shouldFix.title: The component-tail repair conflates the DR-105 PT-FS-WRITE-HOST-STATE component token with doctor's unprefixed host operational-metadata write
evidence: The candidate first says EVERY subsequent effect of an admitted CA-1 child stays in DR-105, then explicitly says PT-FS-WRITE-HOST-STATE is host operational-metadata / BLK-6 and is not a component tail. FC-JOIN-COMPONENT-TAIL repeats the same exception.

Both recorded permission generations define /permissionVocabulary/tokens/2 as PT-FS-WRITE-HOST-STATE: bytes inside the host-owned state namespace allocated to this component for its declared state class. Its sliceJustification calls the token the local-write half of D-002's DR-105 scoping, its reversibility text names a direct component write, and /coverageObligation/mapping/state says the token is minted for direct writes.

Recorded doctor-contract.v4 draws the exact actor distinction the candidate loses. /actorMismatch/perConsentClassActorAnalysis/classes/0/componentActorHalf says a spawned component's writes are its own acts and PT-FS-WRITE-HOST-STATE is squarely the right token held by the right actor. /actorMismatch/theDefaultPostureIsInvolvedToo/andTwoOfThemDoNotFitEvenAsWritten says doctor's audit record is allocated to no component, so that PT token cannot express doctor's host act.

Adopted D-032's BLK-6 wording uses the unprefixed FS-WRITE-HOST-STATE label for doctor's operational-metadata write. Adding the PT- prefix changes it into the recorded component permission token; it is not a harmless spelling expansion.

The v4 Claude advisory did not support the exclusion: it listed PT-FS-WRITE-HOST-STATE among the recorded non-egress component routes. v5's predecessor disposition and honesty repair describe the opposite result as repaired.
shouldFix.impact: A fixture generated from the named class can pass while routing a spawned component's direct state write outside DR-105 as doctor/host BLK-6 work. That contradicts the candidate's own EVERY-effect rule and erases the host-versus-component actor boundary for a minted component permission. Because this candidate binds NOTHING and applies no authority, the defect is SHOULD-FIX rather than a blocker.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Keep doctor's unprefixed FS-WRITE-HOST-STATE operational-metadata act distinct from PT-FS-WRITE-HOST-STATE. Remove the PT token exclusion from componentTails and FC-JOIN-COMPONENT-TAIL; either name it as a representative admitted-child DR-105 route or leave the examples explicitly non-exhaustive under the EVERY-effect rule. Correct the v4 finding disposition and honesty-repair recital. Do not reopen BLK-6 for doctor's own host act and do not mint a token.

shouldFix.title: The new one-binding claim is contradicted by retained text that equates the SPAWN subtype with the host-head class
evidence: hostHeadTermBinding says 'Host head' without a subtype means the CA-1-host-head class containing SPAWN and IN_PROCESS, says CA-1 SPAWN is only the SPAWN subtype, and claims this artifact never uses host head as a synonym for SPAWN alone.
honestyRepairsFromV2[1] still says 'CA-1 SPAWN decision is the host head.' That is the exact synonym the new binding says does not occur.

v5 removed the same equivocation from componentTails and hostSideAttemptsOutsideDr105 but did not roster or repair this remaining occurrence. No standing marks honestyRepairsFromV2 as non-governing quotation, and the sentence is a current repair recital rather than verbatim frozen predecessor bytes.

The surviving occurrence is material to CLAUDE-DAJ4-S1: the prior defect arose because collapsing host head to SPAWN could drop IN_PROCESS from class-level deny reasoning. The dedicated IN_PROCESS clause and fixture are correct, but the promised single term binding is not yet true throughout the artifact.
shouldFix.impact: A downstream reader can still select the retained SPAWN-only meaning for host head and reproduce the class/subtype equivocation the v5 repair claims to close. The explicit IN_PROCESS denial bounds current authority risk, and the artifact binds NOTHING, so this is SHOULD-FIX rather than a blocker.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Change the retained recital to say that the CA-1 SPAWN decision is the SPAWN subtype of CA-1-host-head, or explicitly mark the old wording historical and superseded while making the absolute term-binding claim accurate. Preserve IN_PROCESS as classified and preview-unexercisable; do not relabel or admit it.
